arm-A.title: Trinity's escape across the rooftops to the phone
arm-A.summary: Morpheus confirms Trinity's hotel hardline is cut and directs her to a phone at Wells and Lake. She runs the building's exterior to the street — hall, fire escape, roof, across the rooftops, and down through a window into a back stairwell — while the Agents pursue and match her. She reaches a ringing booth on the street and is gone before a garbage truck crushes it, so the Agents are left with wreckage and no body, but with the crew's next target named as Neo.
arm-A.action: After Morpheus confirms the hotel hardline is cut and directs her to a phone at Wells and Lake, Trinity bursts into the hall into Agent Brown and his police unit and flees she plummets through the shattered glass and onto the fire escape. Finding Agent Smith waiting in the alley below, she climbs to the roof and runs the rooftops, clearing a 40-foot gap the cops cannot follow while Agent Brown duplicates the leap with the same unnatural grace. She launches from the roof's edge toward a lit window, dives, crashes through glass into a back stairwell, and — finding only wind where she expects Brown — gets to her feet despite her injuries. On the street she races a U-turning garbage truck to a ringing phone booth, answers it, and is gone before the truck pulverizes the booth; the Agents inspect the wreckage with no body, but leave with the next target named as Neo.

arm-B.title: Trinity's escape across the rooftops to the phone
arm-B.summary: Informed that her hotel hardline is dead and that Agents are on site, Trinity drops the phone and runs for a separate pay phone at Wells and Lake. She slips past Agent Brown's unit in the hall onto the fire escape, is forced upward when Agent Smith blocks the alley, and crosses the rooftops with impossible grace while the cops fall behind and Brown matches her leap. She dives through a window into a back stairwell, crashes down injured but still moving, finds no pursuer behind her, then races a garbage truck to a ringing phone and answers it a split-second before the truck destroys the booth, leaving no body.

state_triples.reading: Trinity moves through this whole run as a soldier converting panic into procedure: the deep breath Morpheus demands in the hotel is the same self-regulation she holds on the rooftop, where calm is not the absence of fear but a decision not to let it touch her hands or her stride. What the arc reveals is that her discipline is exactly what the Agents can match and therefore cannot stop — she escapes not by being faster than Brown but by committing to an exit his power over physics has no answer for

Morpheus is the event's still point: he absorbs Trinity's fear and hands back a single concrete instruction, and his refusal to panic on the line is the discipline that lets her re-collect herself and run. The arc only shows him at its opening, but his voice is the thread the whole escape hangs on — the same calm, directive authority the scene layer notes will later shepherd Neo, so his role here is to establish the guide whose composure becomes the crew's way out.

arm-A.summary: Morpheus confirms Trinity's hotel hardline is cut and directs her to a phone at Wells and Lake. She runs the building's exterior to the street — hall, fire escape, roof, across the rooftops, and down through a window into a back stairwell — while the Agents pursue and match her. She reaches a ringing booth on the street and is gone before a garbage truck crushes it, so the Agents are left with wreckage and no body, but with the crew's next target named as Neo.
arm-A.action: After Morpheus confirms the hotel hardline is cut and directs her to a phone at Wells and Lake, Trinity bursts into the hall into Agent Brown and his police unit and flees she plummets through the shattered glass and onto the fire escape. Finding Agent Smith waiting in the alley below, she climbs to the roof and runs the rooftops, clearing a 40-foot gap the cops cannot follow while Agent Brown duplicates the leap with the same unnatural grace. She launches from the roof's edge toward a lit window, dives, crashes through glass into a back stairwell, and — finding only wind where she expects Brown — gets to her feet despite her injuries. On the street she races a U-turning garbage truck to a ringing phone booth, answers it, and is gone before the truck pulverizes the booth; the Agents inspect the wreckage with no body, but leave with the next target named as Neo.

arm-B.title: Trinity's escape across the rooftops to the phone
arm-B.summary: Informed that her hotel hardline is dead and that Agents are on site, Trinity drops the phone and runs for a separate pay phone at Wells and Lake. She slips past Agent Brown's unit in the hall onto the fire escape, is forced upward when Agent Smith blocks the alley, and crosses the rooftops with impossible grace while the cops fall behind and Brown matches her leap. She dives through a window into a back stairwell, crashes down injured but still moving, finds no pursuer behind her, then races a garbage truck to a ringing phone and answers it a split-second before the truck destroys the booth, leaving no body.

The scene layer reads his flat delivery as the absence of private stake — the quiet satisfaction of a system working exactly as designed — and his 'it's already begun' is the event's closing note of a machine that has already turned its gaze toward the next target.

The Agents function as one jurisdiction rather than three people: they absorb the loss of Trinity without flinching and immediately convert it into a colder victory by confirming the informant and naming the next target. The scene layer reads their coordination as the machine's totalizing surveillance turning outward — and their final image, the camera falling through the phone into a running 'search,' makes the collective itself the event's true endpoint, since the hunt no longer needs a body, only a name.

arm-A.title: Neo is summoned and drawn toward the truth
arm-A.summary: Alone in his apartment, Neo is contacted through his own machine by an unseen party that types messages on its own, answers a knock with the last line, and tells him to follow a white rabbit. When Choi and Dujour arrive for a disk deal, Neo spots a white rabbit pin on Dujour's jacket, and against his plan to work the next day he agrees to go out. At a crowded apartment gathering, Trinity approaches him by name, confirms she was on his computer, catalogs his private habits to prove she has been watching, warns him he is in danger and being watched, and reframes his sleepless searching as the hunt for an answer that is out there and will find him if he wants it, though it must be seen to be believed. She draws him in with a hypnotic, unhurried closeness over the deafening music, then melts back into the crowd, leaving him on his feet in the night, having named aloud the question What is the Matrix?.
arm-A.action: The screens in Neo's apartment go blank and type messages on their own, answering a knock with the last line; Neo trades a disk to Choi for money, then follows Dujour out after recognizing the white rabbit pin; at the gathering, Trinity corners him against a wall and delivers a warning before disappearing into the crowd.

arm-B.title: Neo is summoned and drawn toward the truth
arm-B.summary: Alone in his apartment one night, Neo is contacted through his own PC by an unseen party that types messages the machine should not produce, ending with 'Follow the white rabbit' — and, on cue, a real knock answers the screen. He runs a disk-for-cash deal with Choi and Dujour as usual, but after the visitors leave he can no longer trust whether he is awake or dreaming. Dujour's small white rabbit pin then pulls him out against his better judgment, and at a crowded apartment gathering Trinity — a woman who names herself as the Trinity who breached the I.R.S. database — tells him she was on his computer, warns that he is being watched and in danger, and refuses to give him the answer because it has to be seen to be believed; when Neo asks 'What is the Matrix?' she says the answer is out there and will find him, then withdraws and leaves him standing amid the crowd as a sound closes over him.
arm-B.action: The screen at Neo's PC blanks and types its own messages — 'Wake up, Neo,' 'The Matrix has you,' 'Follow the white rabbit,' 'Knock, knock, Neo' — and a real knock meets the last one. Still unnerved, Neo keeps the chain on, retrieves a disk from a hollowed Baudrillard, takes Choi's 'two grand,' and completes the sale. After Choi jokes the night is mescaline and that he needs to 'unplug,' Neo is hit by a returning 'feeling of unrealness' and asks whether Choi has ever been unsure he was awake. He refuses Dujour's invitation because he has work tomorrow, until he spots a small white rabbit pin on her jacket, at which 'the room tilts' and he agrees to go. At the gathering, Trinity walks straight up to him, names herself as 'the Trinity who breached the I.R.S. D-Base,' confirms she was on his computer, warns that he is 'in danger' and 'being watched,' and, pressing close in the deafening industrial music, tells him he is 'looking for an answer' that must be seen to be believed; Neo voices 'What is the Matrix?' and she says the answer is 'out there,' that it will find him, then melts into the shifting wall of bodies as a sound presses in on him.

state_triples.reading: The setting's only job is to be named: an anonymous tower becomes, in a single line, the ordinary world Neo is being pulled back into — the very office where his small rebellion will be disciplined.

Rhineheart mistakes Neo's vast, sleepless searching for petty arrogance and moves to correct it with the only tool he has — the company's authority — never imagining that the 'special' accusation he throws as an insult is, in a way he cannot conceive, about to become true.

affects_outside.enables: By pinning Neo to his desk under threat of losing his job, the ultimatum sets the terms for what follows: his failure to meet it becomes the ordinary-world pretext that lets outside forces trace and reach him.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: It costs Neo the momentum of the night before — the willing pull toward the answer offered to him is stalled, crowded out by the demand that he conform and be on time.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: The woman who sent him toward the question is absent here; her promise that the answer would find him goes unanswered while Neo submits to the ordinary world.

arm-B.turns_on: The ordinary world reasserting its claim over Neo just as he is being pulled toward the truth — the pivot is whether the vast question or the small demand wins the morning, and for now the small demand does, so that Neo's 'Perfectly clear' is the price of moving through this world untouched.
